name: Cache sized CoreText fonts

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

hypothesisMarkdown:
## Cache sized CoreText fonts

Mechanism: `MacTextSystem::layout_line` made a new CTFont with `clone_with_font_size` for every font run of every line, so CoreText rebuilt the font's ASCII glyph and advance cache each time (44% of CTLineCreate in the data-table profile). Keep the sized font by (font, size bits), bounded at 512. Allowed: gpui_macos text_system.rs. Forbidden: shaping output, glyph rasterization.
measurementPlanMarkdown: bm.sh e09 over eight scenarios against a fresh HEAD run, 3 reps (data-table rechecked with 5). Pass: text-relabel and scroll-data-table shaping cost down, no scenario worse than its noise, new test shows the same layout with the cache cold and warm.
reportMarkdown:
## Cache sized CoreText fonts Finished

Passed: true. Shaping time falls by about half (the CTFontCreateCopy and InitASCIIDataCache frames disappear from the profile), which takes `text-relabel` from 92 to 120 fps with fast mode on or off, and every text scenario gains 0-9% CPU. `scroll-data-table` with fast mode on reads 8% higher CPU over five runs although its draw median is unchanged and its profile shows less shaping; the HEAD runs alone span 2.64-3.17 ms and the new ones 3.02-3.47, run order and thermal drift dominating, so it is recorded as unexplained noise to recheck at the end. New test `a_line_laid_out_again_with_kept_sized_fonts_is_the_same` (4 text_system tests pass, clippy clean).

Attempt Count: 1. Out-of-scope changes: none.
decisionMarkdown:
### Decision

Committed success; re-measure scroll-data-table in the final full run.
